claims.text: PlaceOrderLong.Place checks its input with early returns, sums lines into totalVnd, takes 10% off for a loyal customer, adds a 30,000 VND fee when totalVnd < 2,000,000, prints a saving and an email line, and returns "order placed, total {totalVnd}".
The shipping fee is decided from totalVnd after the discount line has already reduced it, so changing the discount percentage can change whether the fee applies.

Hand trace, loyal customer, one line of quantity 2 at 1,100,000 VND: as written (10%) Place returns "order placed, total 2010000"; with 5% it returns "order placed, total 2090000" (integer arithmetic, 2,200,000 * 10 / 100 = 220,000).
The file's own comment reads: "One method that checks, prices, saves and notifies. Four reasons to change one place, and no name for any of the four."

Design is the set of choices about where each piece of work lives and what it can reach; when code is expected to change after it first works, those choices are a large part of what later changes cost.
claims.source_hint: outline item 3; common definition in software design literature

claims.text: After the discount, the lines that read totalVnd are the shipping fee line, the saving line and the return; the email line prints only customerId.
Whether the shipping fee should use the discounted or the original total is a business rule that PlaceOrderLong does not state anywhere; the order of its lines decides it implicitly.

claims.text: If each rule received the value it needs as a named input, instead of reading one shared variable, a change to the discount rule could not change the fee rule by accident.
claims.source_hint: follows from claims 2 and 6; condition stated in the sentence
